correctness.rationale: The audited RESULT.md defines separate uniform labeled tree laws for each a, fixed total N and two marked vertices in the first part. Disjoint connecting-path events and the Ge–Dong prescribed-tree inclusion theorem give S_k(a)=(a-2)_(k-1)(N-a-1)_(k-1)/(a(N-a))^(k-1). I independently checked that the path mass telescopes to these tails and the identity f_j(v)-f_j(u)=(v-u)[uv-(u+v-N)(j+1)(N-j)]/[uv(N-u)(N-v)]. The bracket strictly decreases on the common positive support; hence S_k(v)/S_k(u) is unimodal, giving at most one positive-to-negative switch. The equal-support exception at N=2m,u=m,v=m+1 has all multipliers positive; all other H>0 pairs have earlier positive difference and later negative difference. Exact integer optimization of H gives first incomparable (11,6,7), fractions 1/420 and 17/2450. The N→∞ limit H/N²=1-3x/2 supports the claimed open x intervals, not equality at x=2/3. Independent rational checker tested complete admissible comparisons N≤90; these finite checks are corroboration, not the unbounded proof.
residual_risks: The claimed mass formula depends on the cited published prescribed-tree inclusion identity; no arbitrary host graph, cross-part marks, or x=2/3 boundary is proved.

value.rationale: The distance law of two distinguished vertices under graph-part imbalance is a canonical random-spanning-tree observable. Its global stochastic-order trichotomy and first unavoidable crossing sharply separate orderability from incomparability; the limit x=2/3 gives a meaningful scaling transition. The contribution is a complete comparison classification rather than a restatement of the known exact marginal formula.
residual_risks: Only marked vertices in the larger/equal bipartition class; no stochastic comparison for general marked placements or sparse host graphs.

final_claim: For larger/equal first parts in uniform K_{a,N-a} spanning trees, two marked first-part distances obey the exact H_N(u,v) stochastic-order trichotomy, at-most-one survival-tail crossing, first incomparability at N=11, and macroscopic transition x=2/3.
limitations: No comparison at x=2/3 asymptotic boundary.
Published exact marginal law is not newly claimed; all-N proof independent of N≤90 checks.
